evidence.note: The film adapts Sinclair Lewis's novel Arrowsmith, published in 1925. The Duke CSPD Public Domain Day 2021 page lists Sinclair Lewis's Arrowsmith among the 1925 books and states that works from 1925 entered the US public domain on January 1, 2021. This layer covers the novel only. The screenplay is credited to Sidney Howard (adapting the novel); as part of the film it falls under the film's own copyright, which is addressed in the print layer, and I did not research it separately.

editorial:
Arrowsmith is John Ford's 1931 adaptation of Sinclair Lewis's 1925 novel about an idealistic doctor-researcher. Samuel Goldwyn produced it, United Artists released it on December 7, 1931, and it stars Ronald Colman, Helen Hayes, Richard Bennett and Myrna Loy. It received four Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture. A creator might want it for Ford's early sound work, for Colman and Hayes, or for its plague-research story.

The rights trap is the film's own copyright. Because it came out in 1931, it is free only if the copyright was never renewed in its 28th year, and I could not confirm that. No complete search of the renewal records was done, and the Copyright Office catalog was not searched. The novel's term has expired, but that does not free the film. Do not treat the print as cleared until the 1958-1960 renewal records have been searched in full.
faq: Is the 1931 film Arrowsmith in the public domain?

Not established. A 1931 film is free only if its copyright was never renewed. No complete search of the 1958-1960 Catalog of Copyright Entries or the Copyright Office public catalog was done. Search both before reusing it.
Does the novel's expired copyright free the movie?

No. The 1925 novel is public domain, so you can adapt the story yourself. The Goldwyn film is a separate work with its own term, and its screenplay, direction and recorded sound are covered by the film's copyright unless that lapsed.
